03 / INSPECT & EXPORT

NIST INSTALLATION · HANDLING REHEARSAL

Load a monitor wafer, read the trace, retrieve it

  1. Pull out the virtual chamber door and its attached tray and seat an inert monitor wafer. The sample's ID and parent revision are preserved.
  2. Close the chamber, then replay the synthetic 4 s triangular fixture. Inspect the peak, rise and fall slopes, and the time at the peak.
  3. Reopen and retrieve. The trace is not a recipe, measured temperature or evidence of a wafer process.
Primary references and coverage

NIST NanoFab RTP-600xp user handbook. The model uses the NIST installation only where the evidence supports it; exact geometry and teaching assumptions are separate.

Nominal case: 610 × 350 × 580 mm, W × H × D, from the OEM metric table, printed p. 112. The taught 25 mm witness, 230 mm joint stroke, connector positions and undimensioned geometry are authored or inferred.

Independent check: the default 4 s triangle yields a 320 °C peak, 0 s peak dwell and +10 / −10 °C/s slopes. The 2 s plateau fixture reproduces exactly its two-second peak dwell. These are arithmetic checks of synthetic input, not temperature validation.

Contracts: bts.inert-monitor-wafer.v1 and bts.synthetic-tc-trace.v1 → bts.rtp-tc-observation.v1. Export contains the source points, channel, witness ID/revision and analytical summary. No process, measured thermal data or wafer change is implied.
